The present claim petition is filed by the petitioners for claiming compensation on account of death of Umesh Kumar, husband of petitioner No.1, father of petitioners No. 2 to 4 and son of petitioner No. 5 (since deceased).

2. Brief facts as narrated by the petitioners are that on 16.03.2017 at about 1:00 pm, deceased Umesh Kumar, after attending Brahaspat Bazar, was going to his native home at Satyam Enclave,
Village Chhapraula, G.B. Nagar, U.P. and when he had almost crossed the road on foot near Bharat Dharam Kanta on G.T. Road at village Chhapraula, in the meanwhile a tractor bearing No.
HR-10J-0263, came from Dadri side, which was driven by its driver at a very high speed and in a negligent manner and hit against the deceased with a great force, due to which the deceased fell down on road and sustained fatal injuries in the accident.

It is further stated that the public persons gathered at the spot and tried to stop the tractor but the driver fled away from the spot Renu & Ors.
Vs. Arman & Ors.
by leaving the tractor on the spot and the said tractor was handed over to the police and deceased was taken to Ganesh Hospital, Ghaziabad by public person, from where the deceased was referred to LNJPN Hospital, Delhi.
3.
After service of notice, all the respondents have marked their appearance and filed their separate written statement.

3.1 Respondent No.1 in his written statement has stated that he has been falsely been implicated by the police in the present matter in connivance with petitioners and thus petition is liable to be dismissed.
It is further submitted that respondent No.1 is totally innocent and has not committed any offence.
It is further submitted that the said offending vehicle was being driven by one Rakesh S/o Sh. Bhullan Singh and the vehicle was duly insured.

It is further stated that under apprehension, Rakesh fled away from the spot leaving the vehicle and one of the labourers i.e.
respondent No.1 Arman on the said tractor (i.e. offending vehicle) and the police later on implicated respondent No.1 in this case as driver of the alleged offending vehicle.
Further, rest of the allegations and averments have been denied by respondent No.1. 3.2.
Respondent No.2 filed his separate written statement and stated on similar lines as of respondent No.1.

3.3 Respondent No. 3 / insurer has filed its written statement and taken the objection that the driver Renu vs Arman And Ors on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117148005/

Arman was not holding a valid driving licence and the tractor was not having a valid permit and fitness for plying the vehicle and thus the petition deserves to be dismissed as the terms and conditions of the policy have been wilfully violated by the owner.
Rest of the contents of the petition are denied.

4. On the basis of pleadings, following issues were framed on 28.11.2019:-
Renu & Ors. Vs. Arman & Ors.
(i).

Whether Umesh Kumar died in a motor vehicular accident which occurred on 16.03.2017 at 1.00 p.m., near Bharat Dharamkanta, Village Chhaprola, G.T. Road,
District Gautam Budh Nagar, U.P., within jurisdiction of PS Badal Pur, due to rash and negligent driving of tractor bearing registration No.HR-10J- 0263 driven by respondent No.1 / Arman?

(OPP) 
(ii) Whether the terms and conditions of the insurance policy of the said tractor were breached by driving it without having valid driving licence?
(OPR-3)
(iii) Whether the petitioners are entitled to compensation on account of said death and if yes, to what extent and from whom?(OPP)
(iv) Whether the petitioners are entitled to interest on the award amount, if so, at what rate and for which period?

The aforesaid issues are decided as follows - ISSUE No. 1 :
9.
In an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is tested on the touchstone of principle of preponderance of probabilities.
It is also the law that the tribunal is not bound by the technical rules of evidence.

Renu & Ors. Vs. Arman & Ors.
10.
In order to prove their cases, petitioner No.1 being wife of deceased examined herself as PW2.

Further, eye-witness Sh. Deepak Kumar has been examined as PW1 and he clearly deposed in his examination-in-chief that on 16.03.2017, he alongwith his mother were present at his sweet shop situated at Chauhraha of Chaprolla village on Ghaziabad to Dadri road, U.P. and at about 1:00 pm,
he saw a red colour tractor bearing registration No. HR-10J-0263, which was coming from Dadri side at a very high speed and in rash and negligent manner and it hit against a man aged about 35 years old on kacha portion of the road with a great force, who had almost crossed the road by that time and was going towards Satyam Enclave.
He further averred that the impact was so powerful that the injured had fallen down in front of his shop.
PW1 further deposed that he made a hue & cry and noted down the number of said tractor and tried to stop the tractor.
He further deposed that one of the public persons chased the tractor on his bike and driver of the said tractor fled away from the spot after dropping the tractor behind.
He further stated that IO of the case had recorded his statement and prepared site plan on his instruction.
He deposed that the accident had been caused due to rash and negligent driving of driver of the aforesaid tractor.
PW1& PW2 were cross
- examined by the counsel for respondents at length and they remained consistent during their cross-examination.
It is relevant here to mention that respondents have not raised any serious dispute to the occurrence of accident, resulting in fatal injuries to victim Umesh Kumar.
It is seen that there was no inordinate delay in the registration of FIR and FIR was registered on the very next day of the accident on the complaint of brother of the deceased.
Further, PW1 has been cited as an eye-witness in the charge-sheet.

He denied the suggestion of Ld counsel for R-1 that he is a planted Renu vs Arman And Ors on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117148005/
4 witness or that he Renu & Ors. Vs. Arman & Ors.
was not present at the spot of accident.
He also deposed that he had seen the driver at the time of the accident.
During his cross-examination by Ld. Counsel for R-2, he clearly deposed that " I can identify the driver of the tractor who was tall having dark complexion ".
No suggestion was given to PW1 that the description of driver as given to him was inaccurate.
No suggestion was given to PW1 was that the offending vehicle was not involved in the accident.

He deposed that the driver had fled away after leaving the tractor at about 400-500 meters from the spot of the accident and further that the driver had fled away after seeing the crowd, which had tried to chase the driver.
PW1 also deposed that he did not see the driver after the date of accident and that he had seen the driver only after the accident.
The charge-sheet does not specify regarding the manner in which the accused driver was traced out.

However, copy of case diary has been filed by the petitioner reflecting that the driver was arrested on the basis of information given by secret informer and further that the person in custody of offending vehicle at the time of accident i.e. Sohanvir Chaudhary, who is relative of registered owner, had stated to t he police that R-1 was driving the offending tractor trolley at the time of accident.

There is nothing to suggest that R-1 was subjected to test Identification parade but at the same time, it is also true that he was not present at the time of deposition of PW1 before the Tribunal & PW1 deposed that he could identify the driver.
No evidence has been led by R-1 to suggest that he was not driving the vehicle at the time of accident.

Registered owner of the vehicle Mr. Ranbir Singh examined himself as R2W1 and deposed on affidavit that at the time of accident,
the vehicle was being driven by one Rakesh and not R-1 and further that Rakesh had fled away from the spot leaving behind labourer Arman on the said tractor and police later on Renu & Ors.

falsely implicated him.
However, his testimony is completed shattered during his cross-examination.
He stated in his cross-examination that on the date of accident, his brother in law Sohan Vir was in custody of the tractor and further that on that day, tractor was in the field of Sohan Vir.
R-2 deposed further that "I was not present at the spot and therefore cannot say whether Rakesh was driving the vehicle or it was Arman ".
R-2 is not an eye-witness to the accident and further he admittedly was not in the custody of offending vehicle at the time of accident.
R-1 and R-2 failed to examine Sh. Sohan Vir to establish that he had any driver by the name of Rakesh or that he was driving the vehicle at the time of accident.
R2W1/ owner Ranbir Singh admitted that he had not employed any driver by the name Rakesh.
R2W1 stated that at the time of release of the vehicle on superdari, he had intimated to the concerned court in writing regarding false implication of his tractor trolley.

Complaint Mark Z dated 20.03.2017 is not proved on record and original was never produced before the Tribunal and in any case, the statement of R2W1 to the effect that Arman was not driving the offending vehicle at the time of accident has no value, once he admitted that he was not present at the spot and further even the vehicle was not in his custody at the time of accident and that it was in the custody of Sohan Vir.
11. After investigation, the police filed the charge-sheet against respondent no. 1/ Arman the driver of the offending tractor trolley.
Filing of charge-sheet against the driver of offending vehicle prima-facie points to his culpability.

ISSUE No. 2:
17.
The onus to prove this issue is on the R-3 / insurer.

The insurance company has examined R3W1 to prove the objections raised by it and to prove that term or condition of insurance policy was breached/ violated by insured as the driver of the offending vehicle was not having valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident.

18. In view of above, this issue is decided in favour of insurance company.

sentences.text: Section 168 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 enjoins upon the claim Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation, which appears to be just and reasonable.
As per settled law, compensation is not expected to be windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance.

A man is not compensated for the physical injury, he is compensated for the loss Renu & Ors. Vs. Arman & Ors.
which he suffers as a result of that injury (Baker v. Willoughby (1970) Ac 467 at page 492 per Lord Reid).

20. In death cases, the guidelines for computation of compensation have been laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Sarla Verma and Others v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr. (2009) 6 Supreme Court Cases 121.

entities.text: Sarla Verma and Others v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr. (2009) 6 Supreme Court Cases 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

Further, the guidelines have been reiterated by the Constitution Bench of Hon'ble Supreme Court in a case titled as National Insurance Company vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors.,
decided on 31.10.2017, laying down the general principles for computation of compensation in death cases.

sentences.text:
The relevant paras of the judgment are reproduced here as under:
"18.
If these determinations are standardized
, there will be uniformity and consistency in the decisions.
There will be lesser need for detailed evidence.
It will also be easier for the insurance companies to settle accident claims without delay.

19. To have uniformity and consistency, the Tribunals should determine compensation in cases Renu & Ors. Vs. Arman & Ors.
of death, by the following well-settled steps: death case Step-1 (Ascertaining the multiplicand)
The income of the deceased per annum should be determined.

Out of the said income a deduction should be made in regard to the amount which the deceased would have spent on himself by way of Renu vs Arman And Ors on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117148005/
7 personal and living expenses.
The balance expired e which is considered to be the contribution to the dependent family, constitutes the multiplicand.
Step-2 (Ascertaining the multiplier) death case
Having regard to the age of the deceased and period of active career, the appropriate multiplier should be selected.
This does not mean ascertaining the number of years he would have lived or worked but for the accident.
Having regard to several imponderables in life and economic factors, a table of multipliers with reference to the age has been identified by this Court.
The multiplier should be chosen from the said table with reference to the age of the deceased.
Step-3 (Actual Calculation)
The annual contribution to the family(multiplicand) when multiplied by such multiplier gives the 'loss of dependency' to the family.
Thereafter, a conventional amount in the range of Rs.5,000/- to Rs.10,000/- may be added as loss of estates.
Where the deceased is survived by his widow, another conventional amount in the range of Rs.5,000 to Rs.10,000 should be added under the head of loss of consortium.
But no amount is to be awarded under the head of pain, suffering or hardship caused to the legal heirs of the deceased.

The funeral expenses, cost of transportation of the body (if incurred) and the cost of any medical treatment of the deceased before death (if incurred) should also be added."
Renu & Ors. Vs. Arman & Ors.

PECUNIARY DAMAGES:
Age of deceased :
22.

but in the FIR,

Satyam Enclave, Village Chhapraula, Gautam Budh Nagar, U.P.
It is not the plea taken by the petitioners in claim petition and evidence that her husband was temporarily residing and working in Delhi and his permanent address was that of Uttar Pradesh.

The Tribunal is mindful of the fact that a person might be having identify proof of a particular place and migrate to another in search of work, without any address proof but in the case at hand, petitioners have nowhere stated that Umesh Kumar was not residing at Ghaziabad address as disclosed in FIR, medical record and claim petition or that Renu & Ors. while he was residing at U.P., he was working at Delhi.

Election I.D.card of the deceased suggest that deceased was residing in Delhi in the year 2015 but there is absolutely nothing to suggest that since year 2015 till the date of accident, he was residing in Delhi only.

In any case,
there is nothing in the testimony of PW2 to suggest that deceased was residing in Delhi at the time of accident.

In her cross-examination, petitioner No.1 stated that her husband was not employed with anyone and he used to earn on daily basis whereever he used to get work and further admitted that the address in the discharge summary of Ganesh Hospital and medical bills /invoices is shown that of Ghaziabad U.P. and not Delhi address, where petitioner claimed to be residing in addition to Ghaziabad address.

them are stated to be dependents on the deceased.

An appropriate multiplier has to be determined for computation of compensation.

This issue was considered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Pranay Sethi & Others (Supra).

Relevant parts of the judgment are reproduced here as under:
"(iii) While determining the income, an addition of 50% of actual salary to the income of the deceased towards future prospects, where the deceased had a permanent job and was below the age of 40 years, should be made.
The addition should be 30%, if the age of the deceased was between 40 to 50 years.
In case the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years, the addition should be 15%.
Actual salary should be read as actual salary less tax.
(iv) In case the deceased was self-employed or on a fixed salary, an addition of 40% of the established income should be the warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 years.
An addition of 25% where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years and 10% where the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.
The established income means the income minus the tax component."
28. The deceased can be considered a self-employed / on fixed salary, in absence of any documentary evidence to show permanent job or increase in income.

In view of the above said judgment, the deceased, who was 34 years of age, an addition of income of deceased to the extent of 40% has to be considered in view of decision of a Constitution Bench of the Supreme Court in the case, National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi and Ors. (Supra).

Deduction towards Personal Living Expenses:
29.
After choosing the age, multiplier and income of the deceased, necessary deductions have to be made out of the income of the deceased towards his personal expenses.

Hon'ble Supreme Court in case titled as Reshma Kumari & Ors. v. Madan Mohan & Anr ., (2013) 9 SCC 65, in para 30, Renu &
Ors. Vs. Arman & Ors.
laid down the necessary deductions towards personal living and expenses of deceased as under :
